title: Fraternity parties, Earl Crum and his mother's house
summary: The band played fraternity parties and balls as carnival revived after the war, through promoter and drummer Earl Crum, whose mother's house on Lee Circle they used for practice.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah. It was Monk played the guitar. I remember he had a hell of a fine guitar. Somebody had bought over in Italy and brought to this country. I think it was Bill Kleppinger. He was one of his good friends. I think Bill lived at his house. He was living on Napoleon and Ronaldette I believe it was. We had quite a vogue at one time. I don't know how it got started, but a few years in there we played for practically all the fraternity parties around Tulane and most of the balls. The carnival season was just getting reorganized after the war. We got in on the ground floor, out through Earl Crum. He was a promoter. He had all the contacts. They used to call him Sleepy. He looked like he was sleeping all the time while he was playing the drums. I think half the time he was. He was a good promoter. Maybe it was better that he was asleep. But he did. I mean his mother ran that shop on Lee Circle there. She also had a few boarders. Her little house is still there. I think it's some kind of a cocktail lounge or something right as you turn the corner.
On the uptown riverside there? Yeah. Another one near the environment. A little Victorian. That's a nice house.

We used to, all the kings, all the parades used to stop there and have champagne when they were living in Africa. And we'd be up there playing music for our own benefit half the time. We did a lot of our practicing in that little house. So I got to know it real well.
